node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Above below beside and between
node.description: Use basic positional words to describe where objects are located relative to each other.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Left right forward and backward
node.description: Use directional language such as left, right, forward and backward to describe movement.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Near far inside and outside
node.description: Describe relative position using distance and containment language.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Follow position instructions
node.description: Follow oral or visual instructions involving position and movement language.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Describe paths
node.description: Describe a path using ordered movement and direction language.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Turn language
node.description: Use half-turn, quarter-turn and full-turn language to describe orientation changes.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Read simple maps
node.description: Use symbols, landmarks and relative positions to interpret simple maps.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Create simple maps
node.description: Draw simple maps that show important objects, landmarks and relative positions.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Map symbols and legends
node.description: Use symbols and legends to interpret and create simple maps.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Grid references
node.description: Use row and column references to locate positions on simple grids.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Routes on grids
node.description: Follow, describe and compare routes on grids using direction and distance language.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Compass directions
node.description: Use north, south, east and west to describe map directions and routes.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Map scale introduction
node.description: Use simple scale information to interpret relative distances on maps.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Locate from spatial clues
node.description: Use several spatial clues to determine a location on a map or grid.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: First quadrant locations
node.description: Use first-quadrant coordinate positions to locate points in spatial contexts.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Coordinate order in context
node.description: Interpret ordered coordinate locations in context without reversing the horizontal and vertical values.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Four quadrant locations
node.description: Locate points in all four quadrants when representing spatial situations.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Coordinate horizontal and vertical distance
node.description: Use coordinate differences to describe horizontal and vertical distances between locations.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Shape vertices as coordinate locations
node.description: Represent vertices of simple shapes as coordinate locations in the plane.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Route changes in coordinates
node.description: Describe a route by changes in coordinate values between locations.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Spatial relationships in the coordinate plane
node.description: Use coordinates to describe relative positions, alignment and distance relationships.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Position is relative
node.description: Position words describe location relative to another object, person or reference point.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Direction and distance describe movement
node.description: A movement can be described by both where it goes and how far it goes.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Turns change orientation
node.description: A turn changes facing direction or orientation even when the location may stay the same.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Maps use symbols
node.description: Maps use symbols and legends to represent real objects and places.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Grids use rows and columns
node.description: Grid references locate positions by combining row and column information.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Compass directions are fixed
node.description: Compass directions provide fixed directions on a map rather than changing with the viewer.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Map scale links map and real distance
node.description: A map scale relates a distance on a map to a distance in the represented space.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Coordinate order matters in spatial contexts
node.description: The first coordinate gives the horizontal location and the second gives the vertical location in standard Cartesian coordinates.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Coordinates represent locations
node.description: Coordinates can represent precise point locations in the plane.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Coordinate differences show movement
node.description: Differences in coordinate values can show horizontal and vertical movement between locations.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Left right reversal
node.description: Learner reverses left and right when following or giving directions.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Position not treated as relative
node.description: Learner gives a position word without considering the reference object or viewpoint.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Row column confusion
node.description: Learner reverses row and column information when using grid references.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Compass viewpoint confusion
node.description: Learner treats compass directions as changing with the viewer's facing direction on a map.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Reverse coordinate order in spatial contexts
node.description: Learner reverses the horizontal and vertical coordinate values when locating points.

edge.rationale: Basic positional words are core components of position language.
Directional words are core components of position and movement language.
Relative distance and containment words support position descriptions.
Following instructions directly practises position and direction language.
Path description applies ordered position and movement language.
Turn language extends direction language to orientation changes.
Reading maps is a core map and grid practice.
Creating maps applies understanding of mapped positions and symbols.
Symbols and legends are key features of map interpretation.
Grid references are central to locating positions on grids.
Routes on grids apply map and grid interpretation to movement.
Compass directions support map direction and route descriptions.
Map scale extends maps and grids to distance interpretation.
Locating from clues practises map and grid reasoning.
First-quadrant locations introduce Cartesian coordinates in spatial contexts.
Coordinate order is central to using Cartesian coordinates accurately.
Four-quadrant locations extend coordinate location reasoning beyond positive coordinates.
Horizontal and vertical coordinate distance applies coordinate location reasoning.
Representing shape vertices as coordinates connects location to geometric representations.
Route changes in coordinates apply coordinate differences to movement.
Coordinates support describing spatial relationships among points and figures.
Early position language often uses objects and shapes as reference items, but it can develop alongside shape identification.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot identify the reference object in a position statement.

edge.rationale: Directional movement language builds from basic relative position language.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot consistently describe or follow left/right/forward/backward movement.

edge.rationale: Relative distance and containment language extends basic position descriptions.
edge.failure_signal: Learner uses position words without a clear reference point or container.

edge.rationale: Following position instructions requires understanding common direction words.
edge.failure_signal: Learner knows words in isolation but cannot act on combined instructions.

edge.rationale: Describing paths builds from following ordered position and movement instructions.
edge.failure_signal: Learner can follow a route but cannot describe the route in order.

edge.rationale: Turn language extends path descriptions with orientation changes.
edge.failure_signal: Learner describes movement distance but not turns or facing direction.

edge.rationale: Reading simple maps requires interpreting relative positions and directions.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot connect map symbols to locations or relative positions.

edge.rationale: Creating simple maps builds from understanding how maps represent locations.
edge.failure_signal: Learner draws objects but does not preserve relative locations on a map.

edge.rationale: Symbols and legends formalise how maps represent places and objects.
edge.failure_signal: Learner guesses symbols without using the legend or map key.

edge.rationale: Grid references extend map reading to row and column locations.
edge.failure_signal: Learner finds nearby regions but not precise grid locations.

edge.rationale: Routes on grids require locating start, end and intermediate positions on the grid.
edge.failure_signal: Learner follows directions but loses the grid location sequence.

edge.rationale: Compass directions refine route descriptions with fixed directions.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats north or east as viewer-relative rather than map-relative.

edge.rationale: Map scale applies route and map distance reasoning to represented distances.
edge.failure_signal: Learner measures a map distance but cannot relate it to real distance.

edge.rationale: Locating from clues often combines grid references with relative-location information.
edge.failure_signal: Learner uses only one clue and ignores constraints from other clues.

edge.rationale: First-quadrant coordinate locations extend row-column grid reasoning into ordered coordinate locations.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats coordinates like unordered grid labels rather than point locations.

edge.rationale: Understanding coordinate order builds from using first-quadrant locations.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reverses horizontal and vertical coordinate values in context.

edge.rationale: Four-quadrant locations require interpreting positive and negative coordinate values.
edge.failure_signal: Learner can plot positive coordinates but not coordinates with negative values.

edge.rationale: Horizontal and vertical coordinate distances require comparing locations in the coordinate plane.
edge.failure_signal: Learner counts signs incorrectly or mixes horizontal and vertical differences.

edge.rationale: Representing shape vertices requires accurately reading and writing coordinate pairs.
edge.failure_signal: Learner plots vertices with reversed coordinates or connects them in the wrong order.

edge.rationale: Route changes in coordinates use horizontal and vertical coordinate differences.
edge.failure_signal: Learner describes movement visually but not through coordinate changes.

edge.rationale: Coordinate spatial relationships build from locating and comparing points and shape vertices.
edge.failure_signal: Learner plots points but cannot describe alignment, relative position or distance relationships.
